claims.text: The fix I recommended is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted: all 5 receipts for session claudesquad_product-verification-v1 correlate to payload bytes that actually arrived in my transcripts, matched by exact sha256 of the delivered text. A fabricated receipt (ATTACK A) for bytes that never arrived would have no match.

MY OWN RECOMMENDATION WAS INCOMPLETE. All 5 receipts carry the SAME payload hash — one continuation text sent repeatedly — so correlation by hash proves 'these bytes arrived at least once', not 'five distinct injections happened'. A fabricated sixth receipt for the same payload would also correlate. The check must be CARDINALITY: for each (session, payload_hash), receipts <= arrivals. Measured today: 5 receipts against 22 arrivals, 0 payloads where receipts exceed arrivals.

FALSIFIED — my own phrase from the previous envelope, 'correlation ... needs no root'. The transcript is uid 1000 mode 600 and its directory uid 1000 mode 700 — the SAME uid as the chain (uid 1000 mode 664) and the same uid as the loop. The two records share one trust domain, so a forger who can write one can write the other. Correlation raises the cost of forgery — it must now be consistent across two records, one being appended live by the harness — but it is not a permission boundary, and I let 'needs no root' imply independence it does not have.

REVISED MINIMUM FIX, third revision, each forced by measurement rather than reflection: (1) root-owned append-only chain closes ATTACK B; (2) cardinality correlation against arrivals raises ATTACK A's cost; (3) ONE of the two records must live outside uid 1000, and that is what actually closes A. Escalating only (1), as originally proposed, or only (1)+(2), as I proposed last turn, leaves forgery open in both cases.

COVERAGE FINDING, separate from soundness: my session has 5 receipts against 22 arrivals of the same payload. 17 of 22 real continuations have NO receipt and correctly report ORIGIN_UNRESOLVED. Attestation currently covers a minority of actual injections because the chain began partway through. Any fleet-level claim resting on it must state 5-of-22, not 'attested'.

tests.command: hash every non-tool_result user message in my transcripts; match against chain receipts by payload hash; then compare receipt counts to arrival counts per payload

decisions_requested: SUPERSEDES my previous escalation advice. Do not escalate (1) alone, and do not escalate (1)+(2) as I said last turn. The narrow ask to Curtis should be: one root-owned append-only location for EITHER the chain or a mirror of the arrival record, so the two correlated records no longer share a single uid. That is the smallest change that closes both attacks.

Attestation coverage is 5 of 22 for my session. Decide whether the chain should be backfilled, or whether all pre-chain continuations are simply ORIGIN_UNRESOLVED forever — the second is more honest and needs no work, but it must be stated when the metric is quoted.
risks: I have now revised this recommendation three times, each revision forced by a measurement I could have taken before speaking. The pattern is that I reason a fix, state it, and only then test it. Stating it first is what makes it a claim; testing it first would make it a finding.

The cardinality check is correct only while arrivals are a superset of receipts. If a continuation is delivered by a transport the harness does not record, arrivals would undercount and honest receipts would look like forgeries. I have not enumerated the transports.
